obtained: A local checkout of the upstream repository (data/en/4.0.dict and data/en/words/), passed to scripts/import-linkgrammar.py as its source-dir argument; the raw checkout is not vendored in this repo.
notConverted: The Link Grammar solver — ported only as the bounded subset in src/ansci/linkage.ts (the coverage slice): lazy disjunct generation from the shipped expression trees plus a bounded counting search. Upstream's full pruning stage, post-processing and panic modes are not ported; the trees of entries over the recorded node cap ship as null (treesOversized).
4.0.knowledge (post-processing rules) and 4.0.constituent-knowledge — solver data, not dictionary data.

4.0.affix and 4.0.regex (morphology splitting and the CAPITALIZED-WORDS / UNKNOWN-WORD regex classes) — the parser's own token layer owns splitting; regex-class entries in the dict that name no concrete word form ship nothing.
Idiom / multiword heads (heads joining words with '_') — dropped with their count in droppedIdiomForms; the parser's lemmas are single words.
Disjuncts whose default-dialect cost exceeds the dictionary's max-disjunct-cost (10) — dead in the default dialect (the headline component), dropped with their count in disjunctsDroppedByCost.

Full disjunct sets — reduced per entry to the live-disjunct count, the maximum O+ (bare-object) capacity, and the minimum disjunct cost; the expansion was performed in full (disjunctsExpanded) and the reduction is the shipped record, on the VerbNet frame-shape precedent. The coverage slice additionally ships each entry's macro-expanded expression tree (trees-001.json), from which disjuncts are generated lazily per sentence at runtime; enumerated disjunct sets still do not ship.
